_comment: Frozen 2026-10-29 from the retired references/fish-intrinsics category: curated family labels per intrinsic name (used by generate_fish_docs.py) and the family notes that category carried. inferred_description_by_name (2026-10-31): descriptions for the 504 names that have no manual page in any installed version; written from the signature and the wording of documented siblings, or copied from a 7.0/9.8 page the 9.8 index does not link. description_by_name wins when both name an entry.

block iteration & identity: Loop with 'loop foreach' over block.list rather than assuming contiguous IDs.
Prefer named groups and ranges for stable selection.
block geometry & motion: block.pos is the centroid; block.rvel is angular velocity.
contact topology: A contact spans two blocks (b1/b2) and owns one or more sub-contacts.
sub-contact mechanics (joint behavior): Joint constitutive behavior lives on sub-contacts; 'block.subcontact.model' is the jmodel name.
See the 'joint-models' reference for each model's property keywords.
zone iteration & topology: block.zone.containing(pos) finds the zone enclosing a point.
zone state: 'block.zone.model' / 'block.zone.prop' read the assigned zone constitutive model and its properties.
See the 'constitutive-models' reference for property keywords.
gridpoint: block.gp.force.unbal is the per-gridpoint unbalanced force used for convergence.
flow knots: flowknot.pp is the pore pressure at the knot. CORRECTION (live 3DEC 9.7.47): flowknot.head is the LIST-HEAD iterator (flowknot_pnt = flowknot.head()), NOT a hydraulic-head value - there is no hydraulic-head intrinsic; derive head from pp and elevation if needed.
flow planes: A flow plane couples to the mechanical joint via 'flowplane.contact'.

structural nodes and elements: Use 'struct.node.disp.global(node_pnt)' for nodal displacement; 'struct.node.disp' alone is NOT a valid intrinsic in FLAC2D 9.0.
Structural node values are central for support displacement and link-state checks.
Use element-specific families for cable, beam, pile, and liner quantities (shell/geogrid types do not exist in FLAC2D).
reinforcement response: FISH intrinsic naming differs between FLAC2D and FLAC3D: 'struct.beam.force' and 'struct.shell.stress' exist in FLAC3D 9.0 but are rejected in FLAC2D 9.0 (FLAC2D has 'struct.beam.moment' and no shell type). FLAC3D 9.7 has BOTH 'struct.beam.moment' and 'struct.beam.force' (all intrinsic names in this file verified present in the live 9.7 'fish list intrinsics' output, 2026-08-13).
Plot 'structure-beam contour force' attribute names also do NOT mirror FISH intrinsic names directly.
Probe live with 'fish list intrinsics' (paginate output) when an expected name is rejected.
Choose local/global force interpretation deliberately (e.g. 'struct.node.disp.global' vs '.local').
zone interfaces: FLAC2D 9.0 uses the 'interface.*' (or alias 'int.*') prefix — NOT 'zone.interface.*'.
Interface data are often node based; inspect active contact state before interpreting forces.
Interface stiffness and strength should be validated against adjacent zone stiffness and expected discontinuity behavior.
object iteration: Use loop foreach over pointer lists instead of assuming object IDs are contiguous.
Prefer named groups and ranges for stable object selection.
position and topology: FLAC2D positions use x/y model space; FLAC3D positions use x/y/z.

Use 'zone.face.normal(z, side)' for face normal vectors; 'zone.face.gp(z, side, i)' for face gridpoints. 'zone.face' alone is NOT a valid intrinsic in FLAC2D 9.0 nor in FLAC3D 9.7 (only the dotted zone.face.* family exists).
Zone face and node orientation differs between 2D and 3D zone shapes.
state and properties: Use 'zone.model(z)' to query the constitutive-model name; 'zone.cmodel' is NOT a valid intrinsic in FLAC2D 9.0 nor in FLAC3D 9.7.
Use property keywords from the constitutive-models reference with zone.prop.
Use groups rather than geometric coordinates when checking staged regions.
mechanical response: Vector/tensor component availability follows FLAC2D/FLAC3D product rules.
Use histories for long runs and FISH intrinsics for snapshots or derived quantities.

grid geometry: Pointer-taking, except spacing, which takes no argument.
field queries at a position: These take a vec3 POSITION, not a node pointer -- they interpolate the field at that point. Passing a pointer fails. (state)
iteration & identity: mpoint.containing(pos) finds the point occupying a position, mpoint.near(pos,<radius>) the closest one, and mpoint.inbox(lo,hi) every point in a box.
creation & deletion: FISH can build and destroy material points directly -- mpoint.create(volume,position) -- which is the scripted alternative to 'mpoint create' / 'mpoint generate'.
geometry & motion: mpoint.vol is the current point volume; mpoint.deformation is the determinant of the deformation gradient (1.0 in the undeformed state).
The vector forms take an optional component index, so mpoint.pos(mp,3) and mpoint.pos.z(mp) are the same value.
stress & strain: Stress initialized on zones survives the conversion: after 'zone initialize-stresses' then 'mpoint import from-zones', mpoint.stress.zz matches the zone value it came from. (state)
fixity & loading: mpoint.fix(mp,dof) reads or sets the fixity flag for one degree of freedom; the command form is 'mpoint fix velocity-x ... range ...'.
convergence (unbalance): Model-level rather than per-point: these take no arguments.

kinematics: Vector intrinsics carry .x/.y/.z component variants throughout.
process sub-namespaces: wall.thermal.* (48 names incl. thermal facets) and wall.fluid.* (49) mirror the mechanical wall/facet namespaces.
clump body: clump.inglobal/clump.inprin convert between global and principal-axis frames; moi has .real (deformable-mass) variants.
templates: Templates are the reusable shape library behind 'clump template create' / 'clump generate'.
On 6.0 the template orientation family is spelled clump.template.axis.angle(.x/.y/.z); 7.0 renamed it clump.template.aangle(.x/.y/.z).
iteration & topology: contact.list.all / contact.num.all include inactive contacts; contact.list takes an optional type-name filter.
model & properties: contact.prop reads/writes contact-model properties by name; contact.method invokes model methods (e.g. bond/unbond on bonded models).
fluid pipe namespace: contact.fluid.* (27 names) serves the fluid-pipe network riding on the contact fabric.
network statistics: Same Pxy fracture-intensity vocabulary as the plot/compute commands.
intersections: Intersections live in named intersection sets (fracture.intersect.set.*).
inlets: The inlet.* namespace was introduced in 7.0; it does not exist on 6.0.
fragments: Requires fragment tracking to be enabled (fragment compute workflow).
domain: domain.condition reads the model-domain boundary condition.
bricks (periodic-space assemblies): A brick is a saved periodic-cell particle assembly replicated into the model with brick.assemble.
6.0 carries only the 8 core accessors (assemble/delete/find/id/list/maxid/num/typeid); the extent / lower.corner / upper.corner accessors are 7.0+.
thermal twin: rblock.thermal.* (24 names) mirrors the mechanical bookkeeping.
servo control: The FISH handle for 'wall servo' stress-controlled boundaries - read/set the target force, gain, and activation per wall.
facets: wall.facet.conveyor(.x/y/z) is the conveyor-belt surface velocity.

dimension_differences.note: MPoint2D exposes 92 of the 100 'mpoint.*' intrinsics; nothing is 2D-only. The eight that go are the z components of the vector accessors (position, displacement, velocity, applied force, unbalanced force). The TENSOR accessors are unchanged -- 'mpoint.stress.zz' and 'mpoint.strain.xz' exist in 2D, because stress and strain remain full 3D tensors there.

verified.method: Re-ran the enumeration probes from Batches 2-6 against the 2D binary and executed the differences in both directions -- confirming that each 2D-only keyword works in 2D and each 3D-only keyword is rejected there.
verified.identical: The 'mpoint' command family is the same in both: 28 subcommands, letter for letter. So are the 'mpoint initialize' field list (25 entries) and the six plot item type names. The command docs need no dimension gating; only the geometry vocabulary around them differs.
verified.resolved: 'zone create2d' was recorded in Batch 1 as absent from MPoint. It is present on MPoint2D (spelled 'create2D' in the keyword table). The original verdict described the 3D binary, not the product -- which is what prompted this pass.
traps: Probing with '?' is NOT side-effect free. 'mpoint generate ?' generated 144 material points and then printed the keyword list. Any command that can run with no arguments will run before it answers. Probe on a model you are willing to lose.
An entry in an enumeration is not a usable feature: MPoint2D lists 'cavehoek' among its constitutive models but offers no way to configure for it.

draw-period: This whole family is undocumented: there is no `fish_massflow.drawperiod.*` page in the 9.7 manual. The signatures come from live enumeration and only `num` has been confirmed against a known model (59 imported periods -> 59).

Semantics of the per-period accessors are NOT established. On a model with 7-day periods computed to day 20, `massflow.drawperiod.find(1)` returned day.start 1 and day.end 1, and `drawpoints()` returned an empty list — neither matches the imported schedule, so do not read these as 'period 1 spans days 1-7'.
`massflow.drawperiod.drawrate` carries a `= flt` assignment form in its signature, but assigning to it on that model neither changed the value it returns nor raised. Treat it as unverified.
Use `massflow.period`, `massflow.period.days(i)` and the drawpoint mass intrinsics for schedule accounting that has been checked.
drawpoint: `massflow.drawpoint.radius(dp, i)` and `height(dp, i)` index the IMZ slices listed by `massflow.drawpoint.slices(dp)`.
`mass.requested` works by day; `mass.actual`, `mass.actual.cum` and `mass.actual.period` report what was really drawn.
`mass.requested` is the scheduled daily tonnage — the period mass divided by the period length. On the tutorial model (2000 per 7-day period) it reads 285.714 for every day of the period.

`mass.actual` is quantised to whole markers, so a day either extracts a marker's worth or nothing: days 1-3 of DP1 read 325, 0, 0 while `mass.actual.cum` holds at 325. Over period 1 the requested 2000 came out as 1625 = 5 x 325.
`massflow.mass.DpDay(1,1)` returned 0 on that same model while `massflow.drawpoint.mass.actual(dp,1)` returned 325 — the two do not agree, so prefer the drawpoint accessors for per-day mass.
extracted-marker: Iterate with `loop foreach local m massflow.extractedmarker.list`.
`massflow.extractedmarker.mineblock` gives the block the material came from, which is what origin/destination reporting keys on.
marker: `massflow.marker.type` returns an integer: -2 unbulked for IMZ growth, -1 unbulked for collapse, 0 unbulked for rilling, 1 partially bulked, 2 fully bulked, 3 air.
`massflow.marker.active.tolerance` is a global setting, readable and writable, not a per-marker value.
An intrinsic whose signature ends in `:= <type>` can be assigned to, not just read.

`massflow.marker.moved-day` and `massflow.marker.moved-cycle` cannot be written in a FISH expression: the parser reads the hyphen as subtraction and fails with `massflow.marker.moved is not recognized as a library function`. They are listed by `fish list intrinsics` all the same.
On the tutorial model at day 20 every active marker was also type 2 (fully bulked): 458 of 1117 by both counts.
mineblock: `massflow.mineblock.state` returns an integer. The manual lists -1 solid, 1 caved, 2 mobilized active, 3 mobilized inactive, 4 air, 5 extracted — but block 1 of the tutorial model reads back **0**, which the manual does not list, and the vendor's own unittests.dat asserts that same 0.
Pairs like `frag.primary.a` / `frag.primary.a.dyn` are the imported value and its user-writable override; when they differ, the dynamic one is used.
Iterate with `loop foreach local mb massflow.mineblock.list` rather than assuming contiguous IDs.
model: `massflow.markerfraglimit.lower/upper` and `massflow.massbalance.lower/upper` are the FISH side of the `massflow initialize markerfraglimit-*` and `massbalance-*` keywords; both are readable and writable.
`massflow.mass.DpDay` is spelled in mixed case by the binary. FISH is case-insensitive, so the manual's `massflow.mass.dpday` resolves to it.

background-node: Background-node intrinsics take two different kinds of first argument and the engine will not convert between them. pos / vel / id / group / isgroup / force.unbal / mass.mult take a node POINTER (MESHPOINT_pnt, from mpoint.node.find or mpoint.node.list). disp / pp / stress take a POSITION (vec3) and interpolate the field there. Verified by executing both the correct and the swapped form: mpoint.node.vel(<vec3>) and mpoint.node.pp(<ptr>) both fail. (state)

The grid spans the whole 'model domain extent', not the material-point bounding box, and is built lazily at 'mpoint import' time. mpoint.node.pos of the first node is the domain corner. Keep the domain tight. (state)
mpoint.node.spacing() reports the value set by 'mpoint node spacing'.
mpoint.node.mass.mult is undocumented -- no doc page and no entry in out_fish.txt -- but the engine exposes it and it returns 1.0 on an untouched grid. (state)
material-point: Material points are not exposed to the Python API. itasca.* reports a count of zero after 'mpoint import from-zones' even though the points exist -- use these intrinsics.
Iterate with 'loop foreach local mp mpoint.list' rather than assuming contiguous IDs.
An intrinsic whose signature ends in ':= <type>' can be assigned to, not just read (for example mpoint.vel(mp) = vector(0,0,0)).
Properties are constitutive-model-specific: mpoint.prop(mp,'young') works only if the assigned model has that property. See references/constitutive-models.
